ei.title: The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

fullPassage:
The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

The Boy Who Chooses an Easy and Familiar Path

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.

"No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway."

In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

The Boy Who Embraces the Challenge

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!

questions.passage: Think of an (A)[ordinary / extraordinary] boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is (B)[excited / exhausted]. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and (C)[challenges / changes] his dad to a match.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 평범한 소년을 생각해 보세요. 차고 안에 탁구대가 있자 소년은 신이 났습니다. 그는 네트 반대편으로 달려가서 아빠에게 경기를 도전합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ordinary — excited — challenges
❌ ② extraordinary — excited — changes
❌ ③ ordinary — exhausted — changes
❌ ④ extraordinary — exhausted — challenges
✅ (A) ordinary: '평범한 소년'이 문맥에 맞음. extraordinary(비범한)는 반대. ✅ (B) excited: 탁구대를 받아 '신이 남'. exhausted(지친)는 반대. ✅ (C) challenges: 아빠에게 경기를 '도전함'. changes(바꾸다)는 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: ordinary(평범한) ↔ extraordinary(비범한). challenge: 명사(도전) + 동사(도전하다) 모두 가능.

questions.passage: Let's start with the path of (A)[avoidance / acceptance]. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and (B)[bruising / brushing] his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the (C)[paddle / pedal] on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 회피의 길부터 시작해 봅시다. 공이 돌아와 팔꿈치에 멍이 들게 합니다. 소년은 탁구대 위에 탁구채를 놓고 방으로 떠납니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② avoidance — bruising — paddle
❌ ① acceptance — bruising — pedal
❌ ③ avoidance — brushing — pedal
❌ ④ acceptance — brushing — paddle
✅ (A) avoidance: '회피의 길'이 문맥에 맞음. acceptance(수용)는 반대 개념. ✅ (B) bruising: 공에 맞아 '멍이 듦'. brushing(닦다/스치다)은 형태 유사하나 의미 다름. ✅ (C) paddle: '탁구채'. pedal(페달)은 형태 유사하나 탁구와 무관.
det.tip: avoidance(회피) ↔ acceptance(수용). bruise(멍들다) vs brush(닦다): 철자 주의.

questions.passage: The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his (A)[opponent / proponent] to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in (B)[triumph / trouble]. This is the true story of Matthew Syed. Because he had a growth (C)[mindset / mindfield], he tried something new and became tough when he faced a difficult task.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그는 상대가 숙련되고 영리하다는 것을 알게 됩니다. 그는 승리감에 공중에 주먹을 날립니다. 그가 성장 사고방식을 가지고 있었기 때문입니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ opponent — triumph — mindset
❌ ② proponent — triumph — mindfield
❌ ① opponent — trouble — mindfield
❌ ④ proponent — trouble — mindset
✅ (A) opponent: 결승전의 '상대'. proponent(지지자)는 반대 개념. ✅ (B) triumph: 이긴 후 '승리감'. trouble(문제)은 반대 감정. ✅ (C) mindset: 'growth mindset(성장 사고방식)' 원문 표현. mindfield는 존재하지 않는 단어(minefield=지뢰밭).
det.tip: opponent(상대) ↔ proponent(지지자). triumph(승리) ↔ defeat(패배). growth mindset = 성장 사고방식(Carol Dweck 이론).

questions.passage: Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside. det.analysis: ✅ ①joined(가입했다): 동아리에 가입한 것 적절. ✅ ②practice(연습하다): 더 연습하고 싶었다 적절. ❌ ③walks(걸어간다): 원문은 'rushes(급히 달려간다)'. 신이 나서 달려가는 맥락에 '걸어간다'는 부적절. ✅ ④challenges(도전한다): 아빠에게 경기 도전 적절.
det.tip: rush(급히 달려가다) ↔ walk(걸어가다). 감정(excited)과 행동의 일관성에 주목.

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he ①<u>turns down</u> her suggestion because his brother is very tough. In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than ②<u>obstacles</u>, and he holds onto the ③<u>belief</u> that they are best ④<u>embraced</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그는 엄마의 제안을 ①거절합니다. 그의 눈에 도전은 ②장애물에 불과하며 그것들을 ③피하는 것이 가장 좋다는 ④믿음을 고수합니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①turns down(거절하다): 형과의 시합 제안 거절 적절. ✅ ②obstacles(장애물): 도전을 장애물로 봄 적절. ✅ ③belief(믿음): 신념을 고수함 적절. ❌ ④embraced(받아들여진): 원문은 'avoided(피해진)'. 도전을 피하는 소년이 '받아들인다'고 말하는 것은 맥락 반대.
det.tip: embrace(받아들이다) ↔ avoid(피하다). 이 소년은 회피하는 경로를 선택했으므로 avoided가 맞음.

questions.passage: An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a ①<u>decent</u> return. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder. The boy learns from his mistakes and ②<u>develops</u> new skills by practicing. He practices hard until he is able to join the ③<u>regional</u> team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the ④<u>beginning</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가끔 ①괜찮은 되받아치기로 자신도 놀랍니다. 소년은 실수로부터 배우고 새로운 기술을 ②개발합니다. ③지역 팀에 합류합니다. 전국 선수권 대회에서 ④시작까지 올라갑니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①decent(괜찮은): 가끔 괜찮은 리턴을 함 적절. ✅ ②develops(개발하다): 새 기술 개발 적절. ✅ ③regional(지역의): 지역 팀 적절. ❌ ④beginning(시작): 원문은 'finals(결승)'. 전국대회에서 '시작'까지 올라간다는 것은 의미 불통. 결승까지 올라감이 맞음.
det.tip: finals(결승) ↔ beginning(시작). 'make it all the way to ~' = ~까지 올라가다.

det.korean: 소년은 인내심과 용기로 성장하고 어려움에 직면하기로 선택할 수 있습니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③courage(용기): 'endurance and courage'로 어려움에 맞서는 자질. ❌ ①cowardice(비겁함): endurance와 어울리지 않음. ❌ ②comfort(편안함): 도전에 맞서는 맥락과 불일치. ❌ ④caution(주의): 도전 정신과 거리 멈.
det.tip: endurance(인내) + courage(용기) = 도전에 맞서는 자질 세트. cowardice(비겁함)는 courage의 반의어.

det.analysis: ✅ ④force(힘/전력): 'with full force'는 '전력으로'라는 관용 표현. ❌ ①speed(속도): 'full speed'도 가능하지만 hitting and bruising과의 연결에서 force가 더 자연스러움. ❌ ②power(힘): 의미는 유사하나 'full power'보다 'full force'가 원문. ❌ ③energy(에너지): 공이 에너지로 돌아온다는 표현은 부자연스러움.
det.tip: with full force = 전력으로, 힘껏. force vs power: force는 물리적 힘, power는 능력/권력.

questions.passage:
The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

The Boy Who Chooses an Easy and Familiar Path

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net <u>rapidly</u>, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.

"No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway."

In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

The Boy Who Embraces the Challenge

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!

det.tip: rapidly = quickly = fast = swiftly (빠르게). ↔ slowly(느리게).

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 성장하기 위해 스스로에게 도전하기로 선택할 수 있습니다. (B) 그의 눈에 시련은 장애물에 불과합니다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) 도전하다: 'challenge himself to grow'는 자신에게 도전. (B) 시련: 'challenges are nothing more than obstacles'에서 challenges는 극복해야 할 '시련/도전적 상황'. ❌ ① (B)에서 '도전'은 너무 긍정적. 이 소년은 부정적으로 봄. ❌ ② (A) '이의를 제기하다'는 법적 맥락. ❌ ④ (A) '이의를 제기하다'와 (B) '도전' 모두 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: challenge: (동사) ~에게 도전하다 / (명사) 도전, 시련, 난제. 맥락에 따라 긍정(도전) 또는 부정(시련) 뉘앙스.

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the ability to continue doing something difficult or painful over a long period of time"

det.korean: "오랜 기간 동안 어렵거나 고통스러운 일을 계속할 수 있는 능력" = 인내(endurance)
det.analysis: ✅ ④endurance(인내력): 어려운 일을 오래 지속하는 능력. ❌ ①courage(용기): 두려움에 맞서는 능력이지 지속력이 아님. ❌ ③avoidance(회피): 피하는 것이라 반대. ❌ ②triumph(승리): 결과이지 능력이 아님.
det.tip: endurance(인내력): endure(견디다) + -ance(명사형). 마라톤 등 지구력 스포츠에서도 사용.

questions.passage: The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it __________. (complete)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 공이 빠르게 날아오자 그는 공을 완전히 놓칩니다.
det.analysis: ✅ completely: 동사 misses를 수식하는 부사 필요. complete(형용사) → completely(부사). '-ly'를 붙여 부사로 변환.
det.tip: 형용사 → 부사: complete → completely, rapid → rapidly. 동사를 수식할 때는 부사 사용.

questions.passage: He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of __________ his game. (improve)
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 수년 동안 그는 자신의 경기를 향상시키는 도전을 좋아했습니다.
det.analysis: ✅ improving: 'the challenge of ~ing' 구문에서 전치사 of 뒤에 동명사(~ing) 필요. improve → improving.
det.tip: 전치사(of, in, at, for...) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing). 'the challenge of improving' = 향상시키는 도전.

questions.passage:
The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

The Boy Who Chooses an Easy and Familiar Path

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.

"No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway."

In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

The Boy Who Embraces the Challenge

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and ____.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 하지만 그는 공을 집어 들고 어쨌든 다시 시도합니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①tries again anyway: However(하지만)로 역접 → 포기하지 않고 다시 시도. ❌ ②gives up immediately: However 뒤에 포기하면 역접이 아님. ❌ ③leaves for his room: 회피 경로의 소년 행동. ❌ ④puts down the paddle: 역시 포기 행동.
det.tip: 'However'는 앞 내용과 반대를 이끄는 역접 연결어. 어려워도 → 다시 시도.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 중요한 것은 여러분이 도전을 받아들이고 달성하고 싶은 것을 결코 포기하지 않는 것입니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②embrace the challenge: 글 전체 메시지(성장 마인드셋 → 도전 수용). ❌ ①avoid the obstacles: 글의 메시지와 정반대(회피). ❌ ④choose a familiar path: 회피 경로 소년의 선택. ❌ ③stay in your comfort zone: 성장 마인드셋과 반대.
det.tip: embrace the challenge(도전을 받아들이다) = 글의 핵심 주제. growth mindset의 핵심은 어려움을 성장의 기회로 봄.
